# Project terminal worktrees (server): create, close, keep, delete ## What to build Today a terminal opened on a **project** (`POST /api/terminals { projectId }`) starts in the shared project folder `/.projects//`. Its `repos/` entries are symlinks to the real workspace checkouts, so nothing is isolated. This slice gives each project terminal its own folder: - **Project-repo worktree:** `.projects/

/.gm-worktrees/`, a git worktree of the project folder's own repo on branch `gm-term/`, cut from the project repo's `HEAD`. - **Repo links:** inside it, `repos/` symlinks point at `/.gm-worktrees/`, one worktree per repo on `gm-term/` (same ``), each cut from the chosen base branch. - **Closing** follows the workspace-terminal rules: no work anywhere → remove everything; work → 409 `needsChoice`; `?worktree=keep|delete`. - **Store:** a new `projectWorktrees` record holds the set. Server only. The spec is `docs/prd/project-terminal-worktrees.md` (Decisions; Requirements → "Git helpers", "Store", "API"). Already in the codebase: - `addTerminalWorktree(wsPath, { id?, baseBranch? })` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/worktrees.ts` fetches `origin/`, cuts from it (local fallback with `warning`), returns `{ id, path, branch, base, baseBranch, warning? }`, returns `undefined` when the repo has no commit, and throws `WorktreeError(status, message)`. - `defaultBaseBranch(ctx, ws)` gives a workspace's default branch. - `GET /api/workspaces/:id/branches` exists. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/worktrees.ts` (whole file) — `git`, `ensureExcluded`, `addTerminalWorktree`, `worktreeState`, `hasWork`, `removeWorktree`, `WorktreeError`, `defaultBaseBranch`, `WORKTREES_DIR`, `TERMINAL_BRANCH_PREFIX`, `newWorktreeId`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts`: - lines 17–152: `createBody`, the `POST` handler (project branch at ~66–70, `newWorktree`, `saveWorktree`, the agent path with `prepareProjectConfig`); - lines 153–186: `DELETE /api/terminals/:id`; - lines 250–290: `worktreeOfTerminal`, `saveWorktree`, `keptWorktrees`, `keptWorktreeRoutes`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/projects.ts`: - lines 1–50: `PROJECTS_DIR`, `PROJECT_FILE`, `projectDirOf`, `Project`, `ProjectFile`; - `LINK_TYPE`, `isLink`, `readProjectFile`; - lines 140–229: `createProjectFolder` (the project repo has `.gitignore` = `repos/\n.graph-execution/\n`) and `removeProjectFolder` (unlinks `repos/*` one by one before `rm -r`; mirror this). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runhome.ts` (lines 60–78) — `projectRepos(workspacesDir, home)` maps `project.json` repos to workspaces by realpath; `projectHome`/`resolveRunHome` build a `ProjectHome`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts` (lines 95–130) — the `terminalWorktrees` zod record with `.default({})`, `TerminalWorktreeRecord`, `store.update(fn)`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts` (lines 10–50) — `TerminalInfo` (`projectId`, `worktree`). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts`: - lines 83–112: a project terminal test (`POST /api/projects { name, workspaces }`); - lines 230–318: worktree tests with real git repos. ## Patterns to follow **Store record** — mirror `terminalWorktrees`: ```ts projectWorktrees: z.record(z.string(), z.object({ projectId: z.string(), path: z.string(), branch: z.string(), base: z.string(), title: z.string(), createdAt: z.string(), terminalId: z.string().optional(), kept: z.boolean().optional(), mergedAt: z.string().optional(), repos: z.array(z.object({ name: z.string(), workspaceId: z.string().optional(), path: z.string(), branch: z.string().optional(), base: z.string().optional(), baseBranch: z.string().optional(), isolated: z.boolean() })), })).default({}), ``` Export `type ProjectWorktreeRecord = Data["projectWorktrees"][string]`. For a non-isolated repo, `path` is the checkout path and `branch`/`base` are absent. **Symlinks** — `await symlink(target, link, LINK_TYPE)` (export `LINK_TYPE` from `projects.ts` if it isn't already). Removing a link: `await rm(link)` with no `recursive`, so the delete never walks into the repo. **Tests** — two real repos under `/github/o/` (`git init -q -b main`, identity, one commit). Create the project via `POST /api/projects { name: "billing", workspaces: ["github~o~a", "github~o~b"] }`, which makes `.projects/billing` with its own git repo and `repos/a`, `repos/b`. ## Step-by-step tasks ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: the `projectWorktrees` record above and its exported type. - **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck` ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/worktrees.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `export async function addProjectWorktrees(projectDir: string, repos: { name: string; workspace: Workspace; baseBranch?: string }[], id = newWorktreeId()): Promise<{ path: string; branch: string; base: string; repos: ProjectRepoWorktree[]; warnings: string[] }>`: 1. Call `addTerminalWorktree(projectDir, { id })` with no base branch, so it cuts from the project's `HEAD`. If that returns `undefined`, throw `WorktreeError(500, "the project folder has no commit")`. 2. For each repo, call `addTerminalWorktree(repo.workspace.path, { id, baseBranch })`: - `undefined` (no commit) → `{ name, workspaceId, path: workspace.path, isolated: false }`; - otherwise `{ name, workspaceId, path, branch, base, baseBranch, isolated: true }`, and push `warning` into `warnings` prefixed with `: `. 3. `mkdir(/repos)` and `symlink(repoPath, /repos/, LINK_TYPE)` for each repo. `repos/` is gitignored in the project repo, so the worktree has no `repos/` folder until you create it. 4. On any error: unlink every `repos/*` link you made, `removeWorktree(workspace.path, path, branch)` for each repo worktree made, `removeWorktree(projectDir, wtPath, gm-term/)`, then rethrow `WorktreeError(err.status ?? 500, ": ")` naming the failing repo. - **IMPLEMENT**: `export async function removeProjectWorktrees(projectDir: string, rec: ProjectWorktreeRecord, workspacePathOf: (workspaceId: string) => string | undefined)`: 1. Unlink `/repos/*` links (only links). 2. For each isolated repo, `removeWorktree(wsPath, repo.path, repo.branch)`. 3. `removeWorktree(projectDir, rec.path, rec.branch)`. Missing pieces are fine. - **IMPLEMENT**: `export async function projectWorktreeState(rec): Promise<{ project: WorktreeState; repos: { name: string; isolated: boolean; dirty: number; ahead: number }[] }>` uses `worktreeState(path, base)` for the project repo and each isolated repo. Non-isolated repos report 0/0. `export const projectHasWork = (s) => hasWork(s.project) || s.repos.some(hasWork)`. - **GOTCHA**: the project-repo worktree's `git status` must not count `repos/`. It is in the project's `.gitignore`; verify this in a test. - **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck` ### UPDATE `POST /api/terminals` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `createBody` gains `bases: z.record(z.string(), z.string().trim().min(1)).optional()`. `bases` without `projectId` → 400 `{ error: "bases needs a projectId" }`. - **IMPLEMENT**: for `projectId`: 1. Resolve the project's repos with `projectRepos(config.workspacesDir, projectHome(...))`. Build the home the way `routes/runs.ts` or `runhome.ts` does; grep `projectHome(`. 2. A repo without a workspace → 409 `{ error: "repo has no workspace" }`. 3. An unknown repo name in `bases` → 400 `{ error: "unknown repo " }`. 4. `baseBranch` = `bases[name] ?? await defaultBaseBranch(ctx, workspace)`. 5. Call `addProjectWorktrees(projectDir, repos, id)` **after** `prepareProjectConfig`, which commits the agent config in the project folder; that matches today's order for workspaces (`newWorktree()` runs after preparation). 6. `cwd` = the project worktree path. Catch `WorktreeError` → `reply.code(err.status).send({ error: err.message })`. - **IMPLEMENT**: the terminal's `worktree` field becomes `{ id, path, branch, repos: [{ name, branch?, baseBranch?, isolated }] }` (extend the `TerminalInfo.worktree` type in `server/terminals.ts` with optional `repos`). Keep `projectId` set and `GM_PROJECT_ID` in the env. - **IMPLEMENT**: save `projectWorktrees[id] = { projectId, path, branch, base, title: info.title, createdAt, terminalId: info.id, repos }`. Add `warnings` to the 201 response when non-empty. - **GOTCHA**: keep `body.cwd`-less root terminals and the existing workspace flow unchanged. ### UPDATE `DELETE /api/terminals/:id` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `export function projectWorktreeOfTerminal(ctx, terminalId)` returns `[wid, rec] | undefined` (open and not kept). In DELETE, when it finds one: 1. Compute `projectWorktreeState`. 2. With no choice and `projectHasWork` → 409 `{ error: "the terminal has work", needsChoice: true, project: { dirty, ahead }, repos: [...], branch: rec.branch, worktreeId: wid }`. 3. Otherwise remove the terminal. `keep` → `delete rec.terminalId; rec.kept = true`. Anything else → `removeProjectWorktrees` and delete the record. - **IMPLEMENT**: project worktrees with `kept: true` or a `terminalId` no longer open count as kept (mirror `keptWorktrees`). Listing and reopening them come in a later slice; this slice only stores them. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts` - **IMPLEMENT** a `describe("project terminal worktrees")` with repos `a` and `b` (both committed) and a third repo `c` with `git init` only (no commit): 1. `POST { projectId }` → 201. `cwd` = `.projects/billing/.gm-worktrees/`, and `project.json` exists there. - `realpathSync(cwd/repos/a)` = `/.gm-worktrees/` on branch `gm-term/`. - `repos/c` resolves to `c`'s checkout, and `worktree.repos` has `{ name: "c", isolated: false }`. - `git status --porcelain` is empty in `a`'s checkout, in `.projects/billing` and in the project worktree. - `.projects/billing/repos/a` still resolves to `a`'s checkout. 2. Closing with no work → 204, and no `gm-term/` branch or `.gm-worktrees/` folder remains in `a`, `b` or the project folder. The `repos/` links are gone without deleting anything in the repos: `a`'s README still exists. 3. Write a file in `cwd/repos/b/` → DELETE 409 with `needsChoice: true` and `repos` including `{ name: "b", dirty: 1 }`. `?worktree=keep` → 204, and the store record has `kept: true`. 4. Edit `project.json` in the project worktree → it counts as work (`project.dirty: 1`). 5. `bases: { a: "nope" }` → 400 naming `a`, and nothing is left behind in any repo or the project folder (rollback). 6. `bases` with workspaceId → 400 `bases needs a projectId`. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts` ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A project terminal's cwd is `.projects/

/.gm-worktrees/` (a worktree of the project repo on `gm-term/`), and its `repos/` resolve to `/.gm-worktrees/`. - [ ] `.projects/

/repos/*` and every checkout are untouched. - [ ] A repo without a commit links to its checkout, with `isolated: false`. - [ ] Any git failure removes everything created and answers with the repo's name. - [ ] Close: no work → 204 and everything removed. Work in any repo or the project repo → 409 `needsChoice` with per-repo counts. `?worktree=keep` keeps the record (`kept: true`), and `?worktree=delete` removes everything. - [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass. ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts npm test ```
